Comment: The absolutive is the unmarked case in Chácobo. Full NPs follow ergative-absolutive alignment with the ergative marked by a high tone (=´) and the absolutive left unmarked (∅).

Pronouns in Chácobo follow nominative-accusative alignment, not ergative-absolutive. The 1SG pronoun is 'i' in S/A function; accusative is marked by the suffix -a (epenthetic case formative). No ergative marking on pronouns.
Same as GB409_2. All pronouns follow nominative-accusative alignment. The split is conditioned by nominal type: full NPs = ERG-ABS; pronouns = NOM-ACC.
Same as GB409_2 and GB409_3. Pronouns are nominative-accusative across all persons.

Full NPs follow ergative-absolutive alignment. The ergative is marked by a high tone clitic (=´) on the NP; the absolutive is unmarked (∅). Example: hóni siri= 'old man=ERG' (Tallman 2018:106, ex. 3.1).

No aspect-conditioned split is reported. The ergative-absolutive alignment on full NPs applies across aspectual contexts. Tallman (2018:32) identifies only two conditioning factors for the split: nominal type and post-clause-type/rank position.
